security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives from markdown examples, public RCSB PDB API URLs, safe file-download examples, and scientific terminology. remediation.suggestion: Clarify that users should choose safe output directories and validate PDB identifiers before saving files.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer requests-based examples or note that subprocess arguments must remain fixed and never include unsanitized user input.

content.value_statement: Structural biology work often requires fast access to public protein and nucleic acid structures. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code search RCSB PDB, retrieve metadata, and download coordinate files.
actual_capabilities: Search RCSB PDB entries by text, organism, resolution, method, and other attributes.
Find structures by sequence similarity or 3D structural similarity.
Retrieve entry, polymer entity, assembly, and GraphQL metadata from public RCSB APIs.
Download coordinate files in PDB, mmCIF, and biological assembly formats.
Process batches of PDB identifiers with rate-limit aware guidance.
Explain core PDB concepts such as biological assemblies, entities, and resolution.
limitations: Requires internet access to public RCSB PDB services.
Subject to RCSB API rate limits and service availability.
Does not perform molecular visualization without external tools.
Downloaded structures may need BioPython or similar libraries for deeper analysis.

use_cases.title: Retrieve structures for analysis
use_cases.description: Find high-quality entries, inspect experimental metadata, and download coordinates for computational workflows.

use_cases.title: Identify target and ligand structures
use_cases.description: Search for protein targets, ligand-bound complexes, and related structures for binding-site review.

use_cases.title: Compare homologous structures
use_cases.description: Use sequence and structural similarity searches to find templates for design, modeling, and mutation analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find a known protein
prompt_templates.prompt: Find RCSB PDB structures for hemoglobin and summarize the best entry, resolution, organism, and experimental method.

prompt_templates.title: Search by sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for PDB structures similar to this protein sequence and rank the top matches by identity and resolution: MTEYKLVVVGAGGVGKSALTIQLIQNHFVDEYDPTIEDSYRKQVVID.

prompt_templates.title: Filter high-quality entries
prompt_templates.prompt: Find human kinase structures solved by X-ray crystallography with resolution better than 2.0 Angstroms and list useful PDB IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a batch workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: For PDB IDs 4HHB, 1MBN, and 1GZX, retrieve metadata, download mmCIF files, and summarize method, resolution, organism, and file names.

output_examples.input: Find human hemoglobin structures with good resolution.
output: A suitable result is 4HHB, human deoxyhemoglobin, solved by X-ray diffraction at 1.74 Angstrom resolution.
Other related entries may be useful for ligand state or mutation comparisons.
Use mmCIF format for modern downstream analysis.

output_examples.input: Download coordinates for 1MBN and explain what I received.
output: The skill can retrieve the coordinate file from the public RCSB download service.
The result is a structure file containing atomic coordinates for myoglobin.
Use BioPython, PyMOL, ChimeraX, or similar tools for visualization and atom-level analysis.

output_examples.output: PDB is the older fixed-column format. mmCIF is the modern standard and is better for large structures and richer metadata.

best_practices: Use search queries to narrow PDB IDs before downloading coordinate files.
Respect API rate limits by batching requests and adding delays for large jobs.
Prefer mmCIF for modern structural biology workflows and large assemblies.
anti_patterns: Do not download large sets of structures without filtering and rate limiting.
Do not assume every PDB entry has high resolution or complete metadata.
Do not use downloaded coordinate files without checking experimental method and quality metrics.

faq.question: What databases does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses public RCSB Protein Data Bank APIs and download endpoints for structures, metadata, and sequences.

faq.question: Can it search by protein sequence?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes SequenceQuery workflows for protein, DNA, or RNA sequence similarity searches.

faq.question: Can it download structure files?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance for downloading PDB, mmCIF, structure factor, and biological assembly files.

faq.question: What is the difference between PDB and mmCIF?
faq.answer: PDB is a legacy text format. mmCIF is the modern format with better support for large structures and metadata.

faq.question: Does it analyze molecular geometry directly?
faq.answer: It helps retrieve and prepare data. Detailed coordinate analysis usually requires tools such as BioPython or molecular viewers.

faq.question: Is an API key required?
faq.answer: No API key is described for the public RCSB endpoints covered by this skill.
